title: 139. The Princes in the Tower Part 2

sentences.en: Grant paused in the act of turning the thing over to consider the face a moment longer.
sentences.zh: 格兰特停下了正把玩那物件的动作，又端详了那张面孔片刻。

sentences.en: A judge?
sentences.zh: 法官？

sentences.en: A soldier?
sentences.zh: 军人？

sentences.en: A prince?
sentences.zh: 王子？

sentences.en: Someone used to great responsibility and responsible in his authority.
sentences.zh: 一个习惯于承担重大责任、且对自己的权力尽职尽责的人。

sentences.en: Someone too conscientious.
sentences.zh: 一个过于恪尽职守的人。

sentences.en: A worrier.
sentences.zh: 一个爱操心的人。

sentences.en: Perhaps a perfectioniSt. Someone too who suffered ill health as a child.
sentences.zh: 也许是个完美主义者。而且他还是个在童年时期饱受病痛折磨的人。

sentences.en: He had that incommunicable, that indescribable look that childhood suffering leaves behind it.
sentences.zh: 他身上有一种难以言喻、无法描述的神情，那是童年苦难留下的痕迹。

sentences.en: He turned the portrait over to look for a caption.
sentences.zh: 他把肖像翻过来寻找说明文字。

sentences.en: On the back was printed
sentences.zh: 背面印着

sentences.en: Richard III.
sentences.zh: 理查三世。

sentences.en: Now that is Josephine Tay's novel The Daughter of Time, published in 1951.
sentences.zh: 这就是约瑟芬·铁伊于1951年出版的小说《时间的女儿》。

sentences.en: It's often described as one of the greatest whodunits ever written.
sentences.zh: 它经常被描述为史上最伟大的推理小说之一。

sentences.en: It's the book that effectively kick-started the kind of Ricardian romance with Richard III, and it is by far the most celebrated attempt to
sentences.zh: 这本书可以说是开启了对理查三世的那种“理查迷恋”，而且到目前为止，它也是最著名的尝试

sentences.en: solve the mystery of the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 解开塔中王子之谜的著作。

sentences.en: Tom Holland, until now, because now the rest is history, will tread in Josephine Tay's footsteps and we will solve the mystery, won't we?
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，到目前为止——因为接下来历史将由我们书写——将追随约瑟芬·铁伊的足迹，由我们来解开这个谜团，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: I'm sure we'll come to this when we look at how people have understood the mystery of the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 我确信，当我们探讨人们是如何理解塔中王子之谜时，我们会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But that thing in Josephine Tay's novel that Richard looks a kind of kind man.
sentences.zh: 但约瑟芬·铁伊的小说里有那么个细节，理查看起来像个挺善良的人。

sentences.en: He's very kind.
sentences.zh: 他非常善良。

sentences.en: So the head of the lady who discovered Richard III in that car park in Leicester, Philippa Langley, she famously said, didn't she, when she saw a portrait of
sentences.zh: 因此，在莱斯特的那个停车场发现理查三世遗骸的那位女士，菲莉帕·兰利，她曾说过一句名言，不是吗？当她看到一幅

sentences.en: Richard III, I think she says it in the documentary, is that the face of a tyrant?
sentences.zh: 理查三世的画像时——我想她在纪录片里说过——那是暴君的脸吗？

sentences.en: Such a kind face.
sentences.zh: 多么慈祥的面容。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I have to say, when you look, because it's a reconstruction, isn't it, based on the body, the skull that was found.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，当你看着它时——因为这是一个根据发现的遗体和头骨进行的复原，对吧？

sentences.en: I think when you look at him, it was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当你看着他时，那真是令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Looks actually rather like Laurence Olivier in the film.
sentences.zh: 实际上看起来挺像电影里的劳伦斯·奥利弗。

sentences.en: Yes, he does actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，其实真的很像。

sentences.en: That's because they've given him
sentences.zh: 那是因为他们给他戴上了

sentences.en: Olivier's wig though, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 奥利弗的假发，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyway, we'll come on to all that.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们稍后会谈到所有这些。

sentences.en: But welcome back to the second half of our episode on the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到我们关于塔中王子这期节目的下半部分。

sentences.en: And Dominic in the first half, basically, he's only just become king, Edward V.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在上半部分里，基本上他才刚成为国王，也就是爱德华五世。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So we should pick up on the 9th of April, 1483, shouldn't we?
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该从1483年4月9日开始讲起，对吧？

sentences.en: So
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: Edward IV has died and he's left two sons, Edward, 12, Richard, 9.
sentences.zh: 爱德华四世已经去世，留下了两个儿子，爱德华12岁，理查9岁。

sentences.en: Richard, he's with his mother, isn't he, in London?
sentences.zh: 理查和他的母亲在伦敦，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, in London.
sentences.zh: 对，在伦敦。

sentences.en: But Edward is in Ludlow with his uncle, Anthony Woodville,
sentences.zh: 但爱德华和他的叔叔安东尼·伍德维尔在拉德洛，

sentences.en: Lord Rivers.
sentences.zh: 即里弗斯勋爵。

sentences.en: And then he has another uncle, Richard of Gloucester, who is basically the boss running the north.
sentences.zh: 此外他还有另一个叔叔，格洛斯特的理查，基本上是掌控北方的老大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Who's up in the north.
sentences.zh: 他在北方。

sentences.en: So the moment that Edward IV dies, there is a degree of, well, there isn't necessarily uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华四世刚一去世，就产生了一种程度的——嗯，倒也未必是不确定性。

sentences.en: Straight away, what happens is a council meets, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 紧接着发生的事情是，一个委员会召开了，对吧？

sentences.en: And they agree, fine, Edward IV has died.
sentences.zh: 他们达成一致，好吧，爱德华四世已经驾崩。

sentences.en: We'll have the coronation of Edward V on the
sentences.zh: 我们将于

sentences.en: 4th of May.
sentences.zh: 5月4日为爱德华五世举行加冕典礼。

sentences.en: But the issue is, he's too young to rule in his own right at the age of 12.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他才12岁，年龄太小，无法亲政。

sentences.en: So obviously, there's some uncertainty about who's actually- So basically, it's four years, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见，关于究竟由谁来——所以基本上是四年，对吧？

sentences.en: So he'll- Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以他会——对。

sentences.en: So not long, but long enough, I suppose, to entrench your networks and to use the power of patronage.
sentences.zh: 时间不长，但我想，也足够长到可以巩固你们的网络并利用恩庇权力了。

sentences.en: Who's going to control the machine between now and then?
sentences.zh: 从现在到那个时候，谁来控制这个国家机器？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Well, there are two things on there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里面有两个问题。

sentences.en: Who's going to control the machine?
sentences.zh: 谁来控制这个国家机器？

sentences.en: And who is going to have control access to the young king?
sentences.zh: 以及谁将获得接触年轻国王的控制权？

sentences.en: Because those are two slightly different issues.
sentences.zh: 因为这是两个略有不同的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we have two questions, which I think go together very well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有两个问题，我认为它们搭配得非常好。

sentences.en: One from Joe Johnson.
sentences.zh: 第一个来自乔·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Was there any scenario in which the Woodvilles or the council could have outmaneuvered Richard to protect the prince's succession?
sentences.zh: 有没有任何可能的情况，让伍德维尔家族或委员会能够智胜理查以保护王子的继承权？

sentences.en: Or was Richard just too powerful and the prince's fate was sealed as soon as Edward IV died?
sentences.zh: 还是说理查实在太强大了，以至于爱德华四世一死，王子的命运就已经注定了？

sentences.en: And Robert Elliot, did Richard have his eye on the crown from the moment
sentences.zh: 还有罗伯特·埃利奥特的问题：理查是从爱德华四世

sentences.en: Edward IV died?
sentences.zh: 去世的那一刻起就盯上王位了吗？

sentences.en: Or was it only when he realised Edward V would never forgive him?
sentences.zh: 还是说直到他意识到爱德华五世绝不会原谅他时才起了异心？

sentences.en: So, you know, massive spoiler alert there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这里有一个巨大的剧透警告。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Of course, everyone listening to this episode will know that Richard ends up taking the crown.
sentences.zh: 当然，收听这期节目的每个人都知道，理查最终夺取了王位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So those two-
sentences.zh: 所以这两个——

sentences.en: Edward V vanishes into the tower.
sentences.zh: 爱德华五世消失在了伦敦塔中。

sentences.en: But was it inevitable that was going to happen?
sentences.zh: 但这是不可避免会发生的吗？

sentences.en: Was Richard always planning to be, to usurp the crown?
sentences.zh: 理查是一直在计划篡夺王位吗？

sentences.en: That's basically the plot of Richard III.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是《理查三世》的剧情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The plot of Richard III, Richard is trying to get rid of everyone who stands in the way of him.
sentences.zh: 在《理查三世》的剧情中，理查试图除掉所有挡他路的人。

sentences.en: You know, he murders everybody.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他谋杀所有人。

sentences.en: And that clearly seems to, I mean, that's clearly not the case.
sentences.zh: 这显然看起来——我是说，这显然不是事实。

sentences.en: But when Edward IV dies, does the news, does Richard think, okay, this is my chance to become king?
sentences.zh: 但当爱德华四世去世时，听到这个消息，理查会想，好吧，这是我成为国王的机会吗？

sentences.en: I would say no, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我会说不会，汤姆。

sentences.en: I would say absolutely no.
sentences.zh: 我会说绝对不会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I would too.
sentences.zh: 我也会这么认为。

sentences.en: I think there's no evidence to suggest that Richard is thinking of becoming king before his brother dies.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有任何证据表明理查在他哥哥去世前动过当国王的念头。

sentences.en: And I would say- Now, the interesting thing is that the common portrait of Richard III is the sort of the Shakespeare portrait.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说——现在有趣的是，关于理查三世的普遍形象就是莎士比亚塑造的那种形象。

sentences.en: He's incredibly cunning and conniving.
sentences.zh: 他极其狡猾奸诈。

sentences.en: And he's planning everything long in advance.
sentences.zh: 而且他很久以前就在筹划一切。

sentences.en: He's playing a very long game.
sentences.zh: 他在下一盘很大的棋。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有任何证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: I think he is-
sentences.zh: 我认为他——

sentences.en: He's as short as everybody else.
sentences.zh: 他和其他所有人一样措手不及。

sentences.en: From the moment his brother dies, he is scrambling, as they all are, to find their place in the new world.
sentences.zh: 从他哥哥去世的那一刻起，他和所有人一样，在新的世界里争先恐后地寻找自己的位置。

sentences.en: And he's constantly improvising.
sentences.zh: 他一直在临场应变。

sentences.en: I think some of his biographers have pointed this out, that actually, he doesn't seem to have a long-term strategy.
sentences.zh: 我想他的一些传记作家已经指出这一点，实际上，他似乎并没有一个长期的战略。

sentences.en: He is constantly grasping for kind of short-term solutions, which often cause then problems of their own further down the line.
sentences.zh: 他一直在抓取某种短期的解决方案，而这些方案往往会在以后引发他们自己的问题。

sentences.en: So he'll make and break alliances, pick people up and drop them, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以他会结盟又毁约，拉拢又抛弃，诸如此类。

sentences.en: However, there is kind of a warning from history from the reign of Henry VI, who, of course, was even younger than Edward V.
sentences.zh: 然而，历史上来自亨利六世统治时期的一个警告——当然，亨利六世比爱德华五世还要年轻。

sentences.en: So he had to have a kind of protector.
sentences.zh: 所以他不得不设立某种摄政。

sentences.en: And that role was taken on by Humphrey, the Duke of Gloucester, who's the youngest brother of Henry V.
sentences.zh: 这个角色由格洛斯特公爵汉弗莱担任，他是亨利五世的小弟弟。

sentences.en: And it doesn't end well for him.
sentences.zh: 而他的结局并不好。

sentences.en: His wife gets accused of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子被指控犯有巫术。

sentences.en: He gets kind of dragged down in scandal.
sentences.zh: 他被卷入了丑闻之中。

sentences.en: And he's chiefly remembered now for setting up a library in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 现在人们主要通过他在牛津建立了一座图书馆来记住他。

sentences.en: So Richard knows that the role of protector is a treacherous one.
sentences.zh: 所以理查知道摄政这个角色是个充满背叛的危险差事。

sentences.en: And it's all the more treacherous if there are kind of rival factions who hate you.
sentences.zh: 如果有充满敌意的敌对派系存在，那就更加危机四伏了。

sentences.en: Yeah, the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，问题就在这里，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Joe Johnson's question about could the Woodvilles have outmanoeuvred Richard?
sentences.zh: 乔·约翰逊关于伍德维尔家族是否能智胜理查的问题。

sentences.en: Now, maybe you'll disagree with me about this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 现在，也许你会在这方面不同意我的看法，汤姆。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I would say, yes, there clearly is a scenario in which the Woodvilles win the day.
sentences.zh: 我会说，是的，显然存在一种伍德维尔家族获胜的情况。

sentences.en: And I would say that by not by looking backwards, but by looking forwards, as we did a little bit in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 而我的观点不是通过回顾过去，而是通过展望未来，正如我们在上一集里稍微做过的那样。

sentences.en: So this is not massively dissimilar from the position when Henry VIII dies.
sentences.zh: 所以这和亨利八世去世时的处境没有本质上的巨大差异。

sentences.en: He also has a very young heir in Edward VI, who has a parvenu family around him, the Seymours.
sentences.zh: 他也有一个非常年轻的继承人爱德华六世，身边围绕着一个暴发户家族——西摩家族。

sentences.en: Now, what happens with Henry VIII and that succession?
sentences.zh: 那么亨利八世和那个继承权问题上发生了什么？

sentences.en: He takes longer to die.
sentences.zh: 他花了更长的时间才去世。

sentences.en: So the Seymours have lots of time to get all their kind of their forces lined up.
sentences.zh: 所以西摩家族有充足的时间把他们各种势力排兵布阵好。

sentences.en: They also have a little bit of a coup before Henry VIII dies to get rid of their factional rival, the Duke of Norfolk and stuff.
sentences.zh: 在亨利八世死前，他们还发动了一场小型政变，以清除他们的派系对手诺福克公爵等人。

sentences.en: So as soon as Henry VIII dies, they move into position, their troops seal off roads, they take possession of the young king, they sort it all out, and basically, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦亨利八世驾崩，他们就进入了位置，他们的军队封锁了道路，他们控制了年轻的国王，把一切都安排妥当，基本上，你知道，

sentences.en: it's fine.
sentences.zh: 一切顺利。

sentences.en: They win the day.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了胜利。

sentences.en: Now, the Woodvilles don't do that, I think, partly because they don't have time, but also arguably because they are less ruthless.
sentences.zh: 现在，伍德维尔家族没有那样做，我认为，部分原因是因为他们没有时间，但也可以说是由于他们不够冷酷。

sentences.en: They are insufficiently ruthless, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我会说他们不够冷酷无情。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: They don't identify Richard as a – they don't identify two people.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把理查识别为——他们没有识别出两个人。

sentences.en: One is Richard, and the other is a man called Hastings.
sentences.zh: 一个是理查，另一个是一个叫黑斯廷斯的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think a further reason why they can't coordinate is that the two key Woodvilles, so Elizabeth, the Queen, and Anthony, her brother, are separate.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们无法协调的另一个原因是，两个关键的伍德维尔家族成员，即王后伊丽莎白和她的兄弟安东尼，是分处两地的。

sentences.en: The Queen is in London, and Anthony, Lord Rivers, is in Ludlow.
sentences.zh: 王后在伦敦，而安东尼，即里弗斯勋爵，在拉德洛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's a big problem that he's in Ludlow.
sentences.zh: 他在拉德洛是个大问题。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Hastings.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了黑斯廷斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, he'd been at Chamberlain.
sentences.zh: 对，他曾担任内侍。

sentences.en: Sorry, I didn't finish my sentence.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我没把话说完。

sentences.en: So Hastings is – so the big – we've talked about the rivalries between the Woodvilles and Richard, which obviously are the kind of titanic ones.
sentences.zh: 所以黑斯廷斯是——最大的——我们讨论过伍德维尔家族与理查之间的敌对关系，这显然是那种惊天动地的矛盾。

sentences.en: But there are other factions within the Yorkist court as well.
sentences.zh: 但约克王朝宫廷内部还有其他派系。

sentences.en: And Hastings is a key player.
sentences.zh: 黑斯廷斯是一个关键人物。

sentences.en: He's been a kind of loyal supporter of Edward IV right the way through.
sentences.zh: 他一直都是爱德华四世的忠实支持者。

sentences.en: In fact, he kind of takes a bribe from Elizabeth Woodville right back in 1464 when she is angling to meet Edward IV.
sentences.zh: 事实上，早在1464年伊丽莎白·伍德维尔急于见爱德华四世时，他就收受了她的贿赂。

sentences.en: And ever since then, there's been kind of tension between them.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他们之间一直存在着某种紧张关系。

sentences.en: But she – Elizabeth Woodville and Hastings do kind of try and arrive at an accommodation.
sentences.zh: 但她——伊丽莎白·伍德维尔和黑斯廷斯确实试图达成某种妥协。

sentences.en: Obviously, they can't do it with reference to Richard because he's up in the north.
sentences.zh: 很显然，他们无法在涉及理查的情况下做到这一点，因为他在北方。

sentences.en: But they kind of arrive at an agreement that all the people who come into London should have small retinues.
sentences.zh: 但他们达成了一种协议，即所有来到伦敦的人都应只带少量的随从。

sentences.en: So that you're not getting large armies kind of congregating on London.
sentences.zh: 这样就不会有庞大的军队聚集在伦敦。

sentences.en: Because they don't want another outbreak of the Walls of the Roses kind of scenario where people pitch up with little armies.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不希望再次爆发玫瑰战争那种各方带着小型军队涌向这里的局面。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so that shows that Hastings and the Woodvilles are kind of trying to arrive at an accommodation.
sentences.zh: 这表明黑斯廷斯和伍德维尔家族正在努力达成妥协。

sentences.en: There's a kind of famous scene in Shakespeare's play where Edward's on his deathbed and he obliges all the various factions to kind of kiss and make up.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚的戏里有个著名的场景，爱德华在临终前强迫各个派系握手言和。

sentences.en: I think that's true, actually, Tom, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此，汤姆，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think it is true.
sentences.zh: 我觉得确实如此。

sentences.en: There's chronical evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 对此有编年史证据支持。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just to go back to the factions, with the question we had last episode, is this Edward IV's great sort of downfall?
sentences.zh: 回过头来谈谈各派系，结合我们上一集提出的问题，这算是爱德华四世的一种重大垮台吗？

sentences.en: Is it his failing as a king?
sentences.zh: 这是他作为国王的失职吗？

sentences.en: I mean, my answer to that would be, remember, the factions are always going to be there.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是，请记住，各派系总是会存在的。

sentences.en: There's always going to be all this competition for lands, for estates, for offices that they're kind of often starting at a very, very local level.
sentences.zh: 土地、地产、官职的竞争总是会存在，而且它们往往是从非常非常基层的水平开始的。

sentences.en: You see it in the past and letters and things, this famous kind of medieval source.
sentences.zh: 你可以在过去的文件、信件以及诸如此类著名的中世纪史料中看到这一点。

sentences.en: So it's inevitable there's going to be a degree of rivalry.
sentences.zh: 因此，一定程度的竞争是不可避免的。

sentences.en: The question is, I suppose, what they all have to calculate is, are we all going to, is there anybody with an ulterior motive?
sentences.zh: 我想问题在于，他们所有人都在盘算的是：我们所有人都要……有没有人怀有不可告人的动机？

sentences.en: Are some, when people talk about compromise, do they mean it?
sentences.zh: 当人们谈论妥协时，他们是认真的吗？

sentences.en: If they don't mean it, should I strike first or should I do nothing?
sentences.zh: 如果他们不是认真的，我是应该先发制人，还是什么都不做？

sentences.en: Well, you could absolutely see, did you ever play the game Kingmaker?
sentences.zh: 嗯，完全可以想象，你玩过《王位制造者》这个游戏吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, I know the game you mean.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，我知道你指的是哪个游戏。

sentences.en: Sensational board game, which kind of revolves around all these kind of tensions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个轰动一时的棋盘游戏，基本上围绕着所有这些紧张局势展开。

sentences.en: You know, who do you make alliances with?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你跟谁结盟？

sentences.en: Who do you kill?
sentences.zh: 你杀谁？

sentences.en: All this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And you can see why, you know, this such dramatic material for Shakespeare and then the influence that those plays have had on mafia dramas or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么这对莎士比亚来说是如此戏剧性的素材，以及这些戏剧对黑帮电影等作品产生了怎样的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, it is a very tense scenario.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常紧张的局面。

sentences.en: But so essentially what's agreed is that Elizabeth Woodville and Hastings in London are trying to arrive to accommodation.
sentences.zh: 但本质上达成的共识是，在伦敦的伊丽莎白·伍德维尔和黑斯廷斯正试图达成妥协。

sentences.en: There's the council as well in London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦还有一个议会。

sentences.en: And they're also part of it.
sentences.zh: 他们也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: The question is, what's going to happen to the young king's two uncles?
sentences.zh: 问题是，年轻国王的那两个叔叔会怎么样？

sentences.en: And they agree that they will rendezvous at Northampton.
sentences.zh: 他们同意在北安普顿会合。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Richard and Anthony Woodville.
sentences.zh: 也就是理查德和安东尼·伍德维尔。

sentences.en: Anthony Woodville is bringing Edward with him.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·伍德维尔带着爱德华同行。

sentences.en: And Richard is coming south and they will meet in Northampton.
sentences.zh: 理查德正向南赶来，他们将在北安普顿会面。

sentences.en: Now, Richard is also going to meet another person who we haven't mentioned at all.
sentences.zh: 现在，理查德还要去见另一个人，我们之前完全没有提到过。

sentences.en: Who is the Duke of Buckingham and Buckingham had been Edward IV's ward.
sentences.zh: 那就是白金汉公爵，白金汉曾是爱德华四世的受监护人。

sentences.en: He's a sort of he's a he's a landowner in the sort of in the Welsh marches.
sentences.zh: 他算是在威尔士边境地区拥有土地的地主。

sentences.en: He's got a big place at Brecon called Brecknock.
sentences.zh: 他在布雷肯有个大庄园叫布雷克诺克。

sentences.en: He's a slightly disaffected figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个略微心怀不满的人物。

sentences.en: Slightly on the fringes of the regime, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 稍微处于政权的边缘，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, he, like the House of York and like the House of Lancaster, is descended from Edward III.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他和约克家族以及兰开斯特家族一样，都是爱德华三世的后代。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he has a very, very tenuous, very tenuous claim.
sentences.zh: 所以他有着非常非常微弱的王位继承权。

sentences.en: And he's married to Catherine Woodville, who is one of the Queen's sisters.
sentences.zh: 他娶了凯瑟琳·伍德维尔，也就是王后的姐妹之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's kind of part of the world, but he's slightly on the outside.
sentences.zh: 所以他某种程度上属于这个圈子，但又有点被排除在外。

sentences.en: But he's ambitious, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他很有野心，对吧？

sentences.en: And he was brought up with Richard, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他是和理查德一起长大的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they know each other well.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很了解对方。

sentences.en: But he's never been a player, particularly till now.
sentences.zh: 但他从来不是一个重要角色，直到现在。

sentences.en: Going back, just got a quick question to a quick moment to Robert Elliott's thing about Richard.
sentences.zh: 顺便问一下，花一点时间提一下罗伯特·埃利奥特关于理查德的观点。

sentences.en: Richard, is Richard, as he comes south, is he thinking, right, I need to plan this to get my hands on the crown?
sentences.zh: 理查德在向南推进时，他心里在想：好吧，我需要计划一下怎么把王冠弄到手吗？

sentences.en: I would say no.
sentences.zh: 我会说没有。

sentences.en: I would say Richard- I think he's planning, I need to get my hands on the king.
sentences.zh: 我会说理查德——我想他在盘算的是：我得把国王控制在手里。

sentences.en: What he's thinking is, he's been running the North.
sentences.zh: 他心里想的是，他一直在治理北方。

sentences.en: He has all his people that he knows in the North and people who owe him loyalty.
sentences.zh: 他在北方有所有他认识的人，还有效忠于他的人。

sentences.en: And he owes them his protection.
sentences.zh: 而他则要为他们提供保护。

sentences.en: You know, that's the way this works.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事情就是这样的。

sentences.en: That's the way the system works.
sentences.zh: 体制就是这样运转的。

sentences.en: So his guiding principle, I think,
sentences.zh: 所以我想他的指导原则是，

sentences.en: is how can I protect my own position and make sure that I don't end up being killed and my people stripped of all their estates and my family thrown out in the cold?
sentences.zh: 我该如何保护自己的地位，确保自己不会最终被杀，我的人民失去所有地产，我的家族被赶尽杀绝？

sentences.en: I think that's what's driving him.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是驱动他的动力。

sentences.en: They're all driven as much, I think, by fear as they are by greed or ambition or any of those things.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们受到的恐惧的驱动，和受贪婪、野心或任何这些东西的驱动一样多。

sentences.en: And I think there's no question as to what his answer to that question is, which to begin with is not to take the crown himself, but to take control of the young king.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他对那个问题的回答一开始不是自己夺取王位，而是控制年轻的国王。

sentences.en: And we know that because of what happens, which is that on the 29th of April, they all meet up at Stony Stratford, which is just outside.
sentences.zh: 我们从随后的事情中知道了这一点，那就是在4月29日，他们在城外的斯托尼斯特拉特福会合。

sentences.en: Well, the Woodvilles are in Stony Stratford, but this is Richard actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伍德维尔家族在斯托尼斯特拉特福，但其实这是理查德。

sentences.en: He's in Northampton, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在北安普顿，对吧？

sentences.en: Richard is – and Buckingham arrives late.
sentences.zh: 理查德在——白金汉迟到了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Richard and Buckingham kind of plot.
sentences.zh: 然后理查德和白金汉进行了密谋。

sentences.en: Well, so Richard's already met.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以理查德已经见过了。

sentences.en: So the Woodvilles, they've left Edward at Stony Stratford with his retinue.
sentences.zh: 所以伍德维尔家族把爱德华和他的随从留在了斯托尼斯特拉特福。

sentences.en: They go into Northampton for a meeting with Richard.
sentences.zh: 他们前往北安普顿与理查德会面。

sentences.en: And apparently at that meeting, he has a very cheerful and merry face.
sentences.zh: 据说在那个会议上，他满面春风，十分愉快。

sentences.en: So that all seems to go well.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切似乎进展顺利。

sentences.en: Buckingham arrives late.
sentences.zh: 白金汉迟到了。

sentences.en: And then we know that Richard and Buckingham sit up late into the night talking.
sentences.zh: 然后我们知道理查德和白金汉彻夜长谈。

sentences.en: And then – And the next morning.
sentences.zh: 然后——第二天早上。

sentences.en: The next morning, everything changes, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，一切都变了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Anthony Woodville wakes up to find that his bed and breakfast, his Airbnb is surrounded.
sentences.zh: 因此，安东尼·伍德维尔醒来时发现他的住处、他的爱彼迎周围被包围了。

sentences.en: So too does Edward V's half-brother, Sir Richard Gray.
sentences.zh: 爱德华五世的同母异父兄弟理查德·格雷爵士也是如此。

sentences.en: So the youngest son of Elizabeth Woodville before she married Edward IV.
sentences.zh: 也就是伊丽莎白·伍德维尔在嫁给爱德华四世之前生的小儿子。

sentences.en: And they're arrested.
sentences.zh: 他们被捕了。

sentences.en: And Richard and Buckingham go to see Edward V.
sentences.zh: 理查德和白金汉去见爱德华五世。

sentences.en: And they say that Rivers was not just a traitor, but morally disreputable.
sentences.zh: 他们说里弗斯不仅是个叛徒，而且道德败坏。

sentences.en: And this is something that Richard is very, very keen on.
sentences.zh: 这是理查德非常非常看重的一点。

sentences.en: He's very hostile to displays of vice and very, very keen on kind of playing the defender of morality.
sentences.zh: 他极其厌恶恶习的展现，并且非常热衷于扮演道德捍卫者。

sentences.en: Well, clearly, by the standards of the day, although he has illegitimate children, he's quite a prurient kind of person.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很显然，以当时的标准来看，尽管他有私生子，但他是一个相当假正经的人。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: That really comes out from his piety.
sentences.zh: 这从他的虔诚中得到了充分的体现。

sentences.en: But I think it's clear that Anthony Woodville was an effective guardian.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很显然，安东尼·伍德维尔是一个称职的监护人。

sentences.en: And this actually is precisely the problem, because when Richard goes and tells Edward V, your guardian is a disgrace, he's a traitor, we've got to get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 这其实正是问题所在，因为当理查德去告诉爱德华五世时：你的监护人是个耻辱，他是个叛徒，我们必须除掉他。

sentences.en: But it's fine, you're now – I'm going to look after you.
sentences.zh: 但没关系，你现在——我会照顾你的。

sentences.en: Edward V says, no.
sentences.zh: 爱德华五世说，不。

sentences.en: He was great.
sentences.zh: 他很好。

sentences.en: I think he's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他棒极了。

sentences.en: I love him.
sentences.zh: 我爱他。

sentences.en: There's a point here, isn't there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 这里有个关键点，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I think this is the key moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最关键的时刻。

sentences.en: Isn't there a point here, though, where it occurred to me, if Edward V had been younger, this wouldn't have been so much of a problem?
sentences.zh: 这里难道不是有一个问题吗，我当时想，如果爱德华五世更小一些，这大概就不会成为这么大的问题了？

sentences.en: So if he'd been five, he would have sort of said, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他当时五岁，他大概就会说，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Oh, fine, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: And off they'd have gone to London.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会动身去伦敦了。

sentences.en: But 12 is quite old.
sentences.zh: 但12岁已经挺大了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And clearly, he just listens to what his uncle, who he hasn't probably seen that much of.
sentences.zh: 很显然，他只听从他的叔叔的话，而他跟这个叔叔可能没见过多少面。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 根本没见过。

sentences.en: Well, he's listened to his other uncle, River.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他听从了他的另一个叔叔里弗斯的话。

sentences.en: The problem is that he sides with Rivers.
sentences.zh: 问题在于他站在了里弗斯那边。

sentences.en: Yeah, clearly.
sentences.zh: 是的，很显然。

sentences.en: And this is a problem for Richard.
sentences.zh: 这对理查德来说是个问题。

sentences.en: That's a definite problem.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个问题。

sentences.en: And I think that everything, everything follows from that.
sentences.zh: 我认为一切，一切都是由此引发的。

sentences.en: Because the fact that Richard is confronted with the nightmare prospect that, you know, the lessons of history teach him, which is that once a king comes of age, it's very,
sentences.zh: 因为理查德面临着一个噩梦般的前景，历史的教训告诉他，一旦国王成年，对摄政王来说就是非常、

sentences.en: very bad news for the protector.
sentences.zh: 非常糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: And especially if there are rival factions.
sentences.zh: 特别是当存在敌对派系的时候。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, I'll tell you a quick fact, by the way, about this coup in Northamptonshire.
sentences.zh: 现在，汤姆，顺便告诉你一个关于北安普顿郡这场政变的小事实。

sentences.en: So the key family around Northamptonshire at that time is a family called the Wake family.
sentences.zh: 当时北安普顿郡周边的核心家族是一个叫韦克家族的家族。

sentences.en: If you've read Tom Penn's book, The Brothers York, which describes-
sentences.zh: 如果你读过汤姆·彭的书《约克兄弟》，里面描述了——

sentences.en: It's a wonderful book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本极好的书。

sentences.en: He talks quite a lot about the Wake family.
sentences.zh: 他在书中花了不少篇幅讲述韦克家族。

sentences.en: They are still in Northamptonshire.
sentences.zh: 他们现在仍然在北安普顿郡。

sentences.en: And the heir to the dynasty is a listener to this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而这个家族的继承人正是本播客的听众。

sentences.en: Oh, goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Johnny Wake.
sentences.zh: 强尼·韦克。

sentences.en: How do you know that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Because his children are at school with my son.
sentences.zh: 因为他的孩子和我儿子在同一个学校上学。

sentences.en: That's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So this is living history.
sentences.zh: 所以这是活生生的历史。

sentences.en: I was very excited when I discovered that.
sentences.zh: 我发现这一点时非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And hopefully he will be too.
sentences.zh: 希望他也会如此。

sentences.en: Although they, since his family took part in a coup that ended up with some infanticide, whether that, maybe he won't appreciate me mentioning it.
sentences.zh: 尽管鉴于他的家族曾参与过一场以虐婴告终的政变，他是否会感激我提起这件事就难说了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so yes.
sentences.zh: 总之，是的。

sentences.en: So Richard has taken possession of Edward.
sentences.zh: 所以理查德已经控制了爱德华。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, we didn't mention that what Elizabeth Woodville is doing with Richard of York, because obviously when word of this-
sentences.zh: 现在，汤姆，我们还没提到伊丽莎白·伍德维尔带着约克的理查德在做什么，因为显然当这个消息传到——

sentences.en: Oh, she's straight off to Sanctuary again.
sentences.zh: 哦，她又直接逃进庇护所了。

sentences.en: She reads the runes.
sentences.zh: 她看清了局势。

sentences.en: I mean, you're a big fan of hers, I know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道你是她的狂热粉丝。

sentences.en: Her brother has been taken off to Pontefract, which, as anyone familiar with the reign of Richard II will know, terrible if you get taken to Pontefract.
sentences.zh: 她的兄弟被带到了庞特弗拉克特，正如任何熟悉理查德二世统治时期的人所知，被带到庞特弗拉克特下场通常很惨。

sentences.en: You're almost bound to die, because that's where Richard II gets murdered.
sentences.zh: 你几乎必死无疑，因为理查德二世就是在那里被谋杀的。

sentences.en: So yes, Elizabeth is straight off to Westminster again.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，伊丽莎白又直接去了威斯敏斯特。

sentences.en: And in a way, she recognises straight away what's going on.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，她一眼就看出了正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And she can see that once Richard of Gloucester has taken that first step, which I think he's taken for completely understandable reasons,
sentences.zh: 她看出，一旦格洛斯特公爵迈出了第一步——我认为他迈出这一步是出于完全可以理解的原因，

sentences.en: he wants to protect himself from the woodfields.
sentences.zh: 他想要保护自己免受伍德维尔家族的侵害——

sentences.en: And once he's taken that first step of securing the king, he's trapped.
sentences.zh: 一旦他迈出了控制国王的第一步，他就被套牢了。

sentences.en: He's on a kind of, yeah, he's on the escalator.
sentences.zh: 他有点像，是的，他踏上了一条不归路。

sentences.en: I mean, you could argue he's been on the escalator from day one, though, couldn't you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你也可以说他从第一天起就踏上这条路了，不是吗？

sentences.en: But what then happens, because again, he comes to London, he goes to the council, and he tells the council to condemn Rivers as a traitor.
sentences.zh: 但接下来会发生什么呢，因为同样地，他来到伦敦，前往议会，并告诉议会谴责里弗斯为叛徒。

sentences.en: And the council basically turns around and says, well, where's your evidence?
sentences.zh: 而议会基本上转过头来说，好吧，你的证据呢？

sentences.en: And it's exactly as when Richard has confronted Edward V, and Edward V says, well, I like Rivers.
sentences.zh: 这正如理查德与爱德华五世对质时一样，爱德华五世说，嗯，我喜欢里弗斯。

sentences.en: But despite that, the council kind of go along with Richard.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，议会还是顺从了理查德。

sentences.en: He's clearly the grand fromage now in the Yorkist court.
sentences.zh: 他现在显然是约克宫廷里的大人物了。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's about a month, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 对啊，因为大约有一个月时间，不是吗？

sentences.en: Fourth of May until the 13th of June, where he's the boss.
sentences.zh: 从5月4日到6月13日，他是掌权者。

sentences.en: Everything seems like it might calm down.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都可能会平息下来。

sentences.en: Do you not think in that period?
sentences.zh: 你不认为在那段时期吗？

sentences.en: Except that two crucial steps are taken, presumably, you know, absolutely led by Richard, one of which is to postpone Edward V's coronation to the 22nd of June.
sentences.zh: 除了采取了两个关键步骤外，据推测，你知道的，绝对是由理查德主导的，其中之一就是将爱德华五世的加冕典礼推迟到6月22日。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's postponed.
sentences.zh: 所以推迟了。

sentences.en: And the other, notoriously, is he should be lodged in the tower.
sentences.zh: 而另一个众所周知的举措是，他应该被安置在塔楼里。

sentences.en: And that's not inherently sinister.
sentences.zh: 这本身并不是什么阴险的事。

sentences.en: That's not that ominous, because at that point, there's no record of killing people.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那么不祥，因为在那个时候，没有杀害记录。

sentences.en: In the tower, particularly.
sentences.zh: 特别是在塔楼里。

sentences.en: I mean, some people have died in the tower.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人确实死在塔楼里。

sentences.en: Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 亨利六世。

sentences.en: Henry VI, okay.
sentences.zh: 亨利六世，好吧。

sentences.en: It is a prison as well as a royal residence.
sentences.zh: 它既是一座监狱，也是一处皇家住所。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think when people hear that about the tower, they think about Henry VIII and his wives, and they think, oh, it means the chopping block.
sentences.zh: 但我想当人们听到关于塔楼的这些时，会想到亨利八世和他的妻子们，然后心想，哦，这意味着断头台。

sentences.en: It doesn't.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: It's the main royal complex in London.
sentences.zh: 它是伦敦主要的皇家建筑群。

sentences.en: I think the scary thing for Edward V, and for people, his sort of pals, is that he is surrounded by Richard's men.
sentences.zh: 我想对于爱德华五世以及人们、他的那些同伴们来说，最可怕的事情在于他被理查德的人包围了。

sentences.en: Richard has total control of him at this stage.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，理查德完全掌控了他。

sentences.en: So he's cut off from the Woodvilles.
sentences.zh: 所以他与伍德ville家族隔绝了。

sentences.en: His uncle is in captivity.
sentences.zh: 他的叔叔被囚禁了。

sentences.en: And he is utterly at the mercy of Richard's guards.
sentences.zh: 而他完全任由理查德的卫兵摆布。

sentences.en: That's the sort of scary thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种可怕的地方。

sentences.en: But at that point, does he think he's in danger of his life?
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，他觉得自己有生命危险吗？

sentences.en: Surely not.
sentences.zh: 当然没有。

sentences.en: Well, Richard wants – so on the 10th of June, he summons basically a massive army from the north.
sentences.zh: 好吧，理查德想要——所以在6月10日，他基本上从北方召集了一支庞大的军队。

sentences.en: So the entire agreement that people wouldn't bring in large armies, Richard parks that.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们不带来大批军队的整个协议，理查德直接把它搁置了。

sentences.en: And we talked about Blackadder.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了《黑爵士》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's taken by Sir Richard Ratcliffe, who is played in the Ian McKellen film of Richard III by Tim McEnany, who's darling.
sentences.zh: 这个角色由理查德·拉特克利夫爵士扮演，在伊恩·麦克莱恩的电影《理查三世》中由蒂姆·麦克纳尼扮演，他非常可爱。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Percy.
sentences.zh: 珀西。

sentences.en: Yeah, Percy.
sentences.zh: 对，珀西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So a little connection there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一点联系。

sentences.en: Three days later, isn't it, that you start to get – you have this incredible scene which Shakespeare famously, brilliantly recreates.
sentences.zh: 三天后，不是吗，你开始看到——你看到了莎士比亚以其著名而又精彩的方式重现的这个不可思议的场景。

sentences.en: Because the other key figure has been Hastings, who was basically the ultimate Edward IV loyaliSt.
sentences.zh: 因为另一个关键人物一直是黑斯廷斯，他基本上是爱德华四世的终极忠诚支持者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And is loyal to the house.
sentences.zh: 并且对家族忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: I think clearly stands for compromise.
sentences.zh: 我认为他显然代表着妥协。

sentences.en: So I think, reading between the lines, what's happened is that in the days – just reading up to this council meeting on the 13th of June,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，字里行间的意思是，发生的事情是，在那些天里——就在6月13日这次议会会议之前，

sentences.en: Richard has probably sounded out Hastings and said, you know, where do we go from here?
sentences.zh: 理查德可能试探过黑斯廷斯并说，你知道的，我们接下来该何去何从？

sentences.en: I could be king.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为国王。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't have to be, but I could be.
sentences.zh: 我不一定非要当，但我可以当。

sentences.en: And maybe that would sort of allow – If the people want me, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 也许这会允许——如果人们需要我，你知道的，随便怎样。

sentences.en: And we could kind of knock out the Woodvilles completely, just take them out of the equation, if I'm king, and you can be number two or something.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把伍德ville家族完全除名，把他们从方程式中抹去，如果我当国王，你可以当老二或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And Hastings probably said, no, I think Edward V has to be king.
sentences.zh: 而黑斯廷斯可能说过，不，我认为爱德华五世必须成为国王。

sentences.en: Because he's loyal to Edward.
sentences.zh: 因为他效忠于爱德华。

sentences.en: He's loyal to Edward IV, and therefore to the line – and ultimately, his loyalty to Edward IV is greater than his hostility to Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 他效忠于爱德华四世，因此也效忠于这一血脉——归根结底，他对爱德华四世的忠诚大于他对伊丽莎白·伍德ville的敌意。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, he is an Edward V loyaliSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是一个爱德华五世的忠实拥护者。

sentences.en: And I think at that point, Richard thinks – it's that classic thing that we saw with Vitalius.
sentences.zh: 我想在那时，理查德觉得——这就像我们在维塔利乌斯身上看到的那个经典情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Richard thinks, oh, God, well, if he's not going to be on my side, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 理查德心想，天哪，好吧，如果他不站在我这边，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: I have to kill him.
sentences.zh: 我必须杀了他。

sentences.en: I have to kill him now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就得杀了他。

sentences.en: And I think that's absolutely what happens.
sentences.zh: 我想这绝对就是发生的事情。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我的意思是，这很有趣。

sentences.en: So, in Shakespeare's play, Richard says, look, you know, I've been bewitched and shows his withered arm.
sentences.zh: 所以在莎士比亚的戏剧中，理查德说，看吧，你知道的，我被施了魔法，并展示了他枯萎的手臂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But actually, what he's doing is he's accusing Elizabeth Woodville of using witchcraft against him.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他这样做是在指责伊丽莎白·伍德ville对使用巫术对付他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's obviously calculated to get Hastings on board, because Hastings hates the Woodvilles.
sentences.zh: 这显然是经过盘算的，为了把黑斯廷斯拉拢过来，因为黑斯廷斯讨厌伍德ville家族。

sentences.en: But Hastings hesitates and says no.
sentences.zh: 但黑斯廷斯犹豫了并拒绝了。

sentences.en: And so Richard hasn't executed.
sentences.zh: 所以理查德没有处决他？

sentences.en: Yes, he does.
sentences.zh: 不，他处决了。

sentences.en: And one of – Hastings's man, it's interesting, the sort of Game of Thrones type dimension, because Hastings's great deputy was a man called Sir William Catesby.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，黑斯廷斯的手下之一带有某种《权力的游戏》式的维度，因为黑斯廷斯伟大的副手是一个叫威廉·凯茨比爵士的人。

sentences.en: And he ditches Hastings at this point.
sentences.zh: 他此时背弃了黑斯廷斯。

sentences.en: Clearly, Richard has suborned him in some way.
sentences.zh: 很明显，理查德通过某种方式收买了他。

sentences.en: He turns on Hastings.
sentences.zh: 他调转枪头对准了黑斯廷斯。

sentences.en: And Hastings is effectively – he's basically dragged out of the council, isn't he, and taken off to the chopping block?
sentences.zh: 而黑斯廷斯实际上——他基本上是被拖出了议会，不是吗，然后被带到了断头台？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And then three days later, again, kind of in the Olivier film, brilliant scene when the young Richard of Shrewsbury is released by Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 然后又是三天后，在奥利弗的电影里，当年轻的什鲁斯伯里的理查德被伊丽莎白·伍德ville释放时，那是一个精彩的场景。

sentences.en: So he's the nine-year-old brother, the younger prince.
sentences.zh: 所以他是那个九岁的弟弟，较小的王子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of a terrifying exchange between them where he – the little boy jokes with Richard, and Richard kind of fixes him with his stare.
sentences.zh: 他们之间有一种可怕的对话，他——小男孩和理查德开玩笑，而理查德用那种目光死死盯着他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Very, very sinister moment.
sentences.zh: 非常非常阴险的时刻。

sentences.en: Whether it seems sinister to people, but, I mean, people must be starting to –
sentences.zh: 不管人们是否觉得阴险，但是，人们一定开始——

sentences.en: Well, presumably at this point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据推测在这一点上。

sentences.en: So Elizabeth Woodville hands her son over, out of sanctuary, to join his older brother in the tower.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白·伍德ville把她的儿子交了出去，离开了庇护所，去塔楼和他的哥哥团聚。

sentences.en: And presumably she does this because she thinks –
sentences.zh: 据推测她这样做是因为她认为——

sentences.en: The coronation is going ahead.
sentences.zh: 加冕典礼将继续进行。

sentences.en: At this point, well, she thinks Richard is clearly determined he's going to be a protector.
sentences.zh: 此时，嗯，她认为理查德显然决心要成为一名摄政王。

sentences.en: He's going to be the big man.
sentences.zh: 他要成为大人物。

sentences.en: The thing to do now is appease him.
sentences.zh: 现在要做的事情是安抚他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, give him my younger son.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，把我的小儿子交给他。

sentences.en: The coronation is still on.
sentences.zh: 加冕典礼仍在进行。

sentences.en: The coronation is still supposedly going to happen on the 22nd of June.
sentences.zh: 加冕典礼据说仍然会在6月22日举行。

sentences.en: But once – as soon as Richard Sr.
sentences.zh: 但是一旦——一旦理查德爵士

sentences.en: has got hold of the little boy, he says, actually, no, the coronation is not going to happen until November now.
sentences.zh: 控制了这个小男孩，他说，事实上，不，加冕典礼现在要推迟到11月了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And at that point you're like, is it ever going to happen?
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候你会想，它还会举行吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then there's a sermon preached on the 22nd of June, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 然后在6月22日发表了一场布道，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Ralph Shaw.
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·肖。

sentences.en: And he says – I mean, they have two arguments, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他说——我的意思是，他们有两个论点，不是吗？

sentences.en: Not even just one, which is clearly a sign that you know your arguments are –
sentences.zh: 甚至不只有一个，这显然表明你知道你的论点是——

sentences.en: A bad one.
sentences.zh: 一个糟糕的论点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So first of all, this guy says Edward IV was completely illegitimate anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，这家伙说爱德华四世无论如何完全是非婚生子。

sentences.en: He was a bastard.
sentences.zh: 他是个私生子。

sentences.en: So Richard basically accuses his own mother of sleeping around.
sentences.zh: 所以理查德基本上指责自己的母亲到处鬼混。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Cecily.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉。

sentences.en: Cecily Neville.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉·内维尔。

sentences.en: He says, you know, she wasn't faithful to my father anyway.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，她对我的父亲反正也不忠。

sentences.en: I mean, Edward IV wasn't even my brother.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，爱德华四世甚至都不是我的兄弟。

sentences.en: And look at Clarence as well.
sentences.zh: 再看看克拉伦斯。

sentences.en: Because he says Edward and Clarence didn't look anything like their father.
sentences.zh: 因为他说爱德华和克拉伦斯长得一点也不像他们的父亲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But I do.
sentences.zh: 但我长得像。

sentences.en: But then the other argument is he wasn't any – and he wasn't married to Elizabeth Woodville anyway
sentences.zh: 但另一个论点是，他根本没有——而且他无论如何也没有娶伊丽莎白·伍德ville

sentences.en: because he had – there had been a pre-contract with another woman, Eleanor Talbot, later Eleanor Butler.
sentences.zh: 因为他曾与另一个女人埃莉诺·塔尔博特（后来的埃莉诺·巴特勒）有过婚前契约。

sentences.en: Who was conveniently dead.
sentences.zh: 而她恰好已经死了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So not only is he a bastard, was he a bastard, my brother, but my nephews are bastards too.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅他是个私生子，我哥哥是个私生子，而且我的侄子们也是私生子。

sentences.en: I think even the most devoted Ricardian has some – you know, it's a guy who's prepared to kind of say that about his mother simply so that he can displace his nephew.
sentences.zh: 我想即使是最忠诚的理查德拥护者也有所——你知道的，这是一个准备为了取代他的侄子而这样谈论自己母亲的家伙。

sentences.en: He's desperate though at this point, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 不过他在这个时候已经绝望了，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Yes, but it's poor form, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这吃相太难看了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I suppose it is poor form.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实吃相难看。

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think that's – that's not filial behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为那是——那不是为人子女的行为。

sentences.en: No, no, it's not filial.
sentences.zh: 不，不，这不是孝顺。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely not very filial behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对不是什么孝顺的行为。

sentences.en: And I think pretty much straight afterwards, the Duke of Buckingham, who's this sort of Weasley figure we mentioned earlier,
sentences.zh: 我想紧接着，白金汉公爵，就是我们前面提到的那个狡猾的家伙，

sentences.en: who's basically attached himself to Richard as chief ally, he goes to the Guildhall, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他基本上作为主要盟友依附于理查德，他去了市政厅，不是吗？

sentences.en: And orchestrates these calls.
sentences.zh: 并精心策划了这些呼喊。

sentences.en: He says, oh, we should give Richard the –
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我们应该把理查德给——

sentences.en: Again, brilliant in the play.
sentences.zh: 剧里演得太精彩了。

sentences.en: The guards all sort of, oh, yeah, what a great idea.
sentences.zh: 卫兵们都一副，哦，对，真是个好主意。

sentences.en: Basically being, you know, given a groat each or something to shout this.
sentences.zh: 基本上是，你知道的，每人给了一个格罗特或者别的什么来喊这个。

sentences.en: And then it's all very swift, incredibly swift.
sentences.zh: 然后一切都非常快，快得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So the 25th of June, the princes are declared illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 所以6月25日，王子们被宣布为非婚生子。

sentences.en: And the thing – you know, the further thing that I think marks this out as deeply treacherous
sentences.zh: 还有一件事——你知道的，我认为这标志着这是极其背叛的另一件事

sentences.en: is that all these rumours about the illegitimacy of the princes and the illegitimacy of Edward's marriage to Elizabeth Woodville,
sentences.zh: 是所有这些关于王子们非婚生以及爱德华与伊丽莎白·伍德ville婚姻非婚生的谣言，

sentences.en: it all originated in the swirl of kind of calumnies and propaganda that had accompanied the coup against Edward back in 1470.
sentences.zh: 都源于1470年伴随反对爱德华政变的那股诽谤和宣传浪潮。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Warren coup.
sentences.zh: 对，沃里克政变。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没毛病。

sentences.en: They're resuscitating all rumours.
sentences.zh: 他们在重拾所有的谣言。

sentences.en: They're resuscitating all that.
sentences.zh: 他们正在重拾这一切。

sentences.en: But is it – Tom, I'm very hesitant to – more hesitant than you are to say, oh, this is terrible villainy.
sentences.zh: 但是——汤姆，我很犹豫——比你更犹豫去说，哦，这是可怕的恶行。

sentences.en: This is – I think all it would have taken would be for Richard to have won one battle and we would be telling this story differently, I think.
sentences.zh: 这是——我认为这一切只需要理查德赢得一场战役，我们就会以不同的方式讲述这个故事了，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: We would be telling it as ruthless.
sentences.zh: 我们会把它描述为冷酷无情。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: And very hard-nosed.
sentences.zh: 而且非常强硬。

sentences.en: But I think we would say, frankly, this is medieval politics.
sentences.zh: 但坦白说，我们会认为，这是中世纪的政治。

sentences.en: This is what Henry IV did to Richard II.
sentences.zh: 这就是亨利四世对理查二世做的事。

sentences.en: It's not, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，其实不然。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 并非如此。

sentences.en: It's exceptional.
sentences.zh: 这是个特例。

sentences.en: Well, the difference is because it's got kids.
sentences.zh: 嗯，区别在于里面有小孩子。

sentences.en: But that's bad luck.
sentences.zh: 但这只能算运气不好。

sentences.en: That is Richard's bad luck.
sentences.zh: 那是理查运气不好。

sentences.en: It's nephews.
sentences.zh: 那是侄子们。

sentences.en: And you think about the other king who murdered his nephew – and I've given away there the fact that I think that Richard is responsible for the murder of the prince in the tower – is John.
sentences.zh: 想想另一个谋杀自己侄子的国王——我刚才已经透露了我觉得理查应该为塔中王子谋杀案负责——那就是约翰。

sentences.en: And the two kings who have had the worst reputations in English history are John and Richard III.
sentences.zh: 在英国历史上名声最差的两个国王就是约翰和理查三世。

sentences.en: And I think it's no coincidence that they were both at least believed to be guilty of the same crime.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他们俩至少被认为犯下了同样的罪行，这绝非巧合。

sentences.en: And you can argue whether they really were, but that was their reputation.
sentences.zh: 你可以争论他们是否真的做了，但这就是他们的名声。

sentences.en: They're totally different characters, though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不过，汤姆，他们的性格完全不同。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, John is famously weak.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，约翰出了名的软弱。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, the thing is that this is not normal behaviour at all.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，关键在于这根本不是正常行为。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's not a normal position.
sentences.zh: 对，但这也不是正常处境。

sentences.en: Of course it's not.
sentences.zh: 当然不是。

sentences.en: Richard is in.
sentences.zh: 理查已经身处其中了。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: And incredibly –
sentences.zh: 而且难以置信的是——

sentences.en: Yeah, he's firefighting.
sentences.zh: 对，他正在四处灭火。

sentences.en: He basically – if he doesn't do any of the steps that he does, he probably thinks he will die.
sentences.zh: 他基本上——如果他不做那些采取的步骤，他大概觉得自己会死。

sentences.en: I entirely accept that.
sentences.zh: 我完全接受这一点。

sentences.en: But I still think that, you know, accusing your mother of sleeping around –
sentences.zh: 但我仍然觉得，你知道，指责你母亲到处鬼混——

sentences.en: It's like the plot of EastEnders.
sentences.zh: 这就像《东区人》的剧情。

sentences.en: It is very – well, all the while, you know, plotting to get rid of your nephew.
sentences.zh: 这非常——好吧，与此同时，你知道，还在密谋摆脱你的侄子。

sentences.en: Your nephew's resuscitating rumours spread about by your own family's enemies.
sentences.zh: 你侄子在煽动你家族敌人们散布的谣言。

sentences.en: You've lost Philippa Langley as a listener.
sentences.zh: 你已经失去菲利帕·兰利这个听众了。

sentences.en: I'll tell you that now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 对，可能吧。

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 可能吧。

sentences.en: But I think it's – and then when you throw into that the kind of – the tone of sanctimony, which I'm sure, you know, is the expression of an authentic Christian sensibility.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这——当你再加上那种假惺惺的语气时，我确信，你知道，那是真实基督教情感的表达。

sentences.en: But it does slightly – it makes him seem an unpleasant figure, I think.
sentences.zh: 但这确实有点——我觉得这让他显得像个讨厌的家伙。

sentences.en: I think we've been – since we've been talking for almost half an hour and you're getting more and more judgmental.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们——既然我们已经聊了快半小时了，而你却变得越来越爱评头论足。

sentences.en: Well, hold on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，等等。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Let's have him crowned.
sentences.zh: 让我们给他加冕吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so let's get him crowned.
sentences.zh: 对，所以让我们让他加冕吧。

sentences.en: So the princes are declared illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 因此，王子们被宣布为私生子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Rivers and Richard Grey are executed at Pontefract.
sentences.zh: 里弗斯和理查·格雷在庞蒂弗拉克特被处决。

sentences.en: In fact, Rivers has written a rather stylish poem and, you know, he's very cool even on the shopping block.
sentences.zh: 事实上，里弗斯写了一首相当潇洒的诗，而且你知道，即使上了断头台他也很酷。

sentences.en: And on the 6th of July, Richard is crowned.
sentences.zh: 而在7月6日，理查加冕了。

sentences.en: And lots of people turn up, but lots of people don't.
sentences.zh: 很多人来了，但也有很多人没来。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Woodville is not there.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·伍德ville不在那里。

sentences.en: And who else is not there?
sentences.zh: 还有谁不在？

sentences.en: Well, Edward V is not there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，爱德华五世不在那里。

sentences.en: Really interestingly, there had been plans for him to attain the coronation.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，原本曾计划让他出席加冕典礼。

sentences.en: They had ordered him clothes and shoes and spurs and horses.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至为他订购了衣服、鞋子、马刺和马匹。

sentences.en: So weirdly, although he'd been declared illegitimate, he was going to attend his uncle's coronation,
sentences.zh: 所以奇怪的是，尽管他被宣布为私生子，他还是要出席他叔叔的加冕典礼，

sentences.en: which I suppose would have been the ultimate kind of affirmation of the new regime, that even the kids themselves accept it.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是对新政权的一种终极肯定，即连孩子们自己都接受了这一点。

sentences.en: But he's not there.
sentences.zh: 但他不在那里。

sentences.en: And at this point, there's a trace reference, which we'll come to perhaps after the break, of him in captivity.
sentences.zh: 而此时，有了一丝关于他被软禁的线索记录，我们也许会在休息后聊到。

sentences.en: But at this point, the princes themselves effectively leave the story.
sentences.zh: 但此时，王子们本人实际上退出了这个故事。

sentences.en: So this is the point, I think, at which we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这就是我们该休息一下的时候了。

sentences.en: And we can return after the break, and we will be solving the mystery of the princes and their tower.
sentences.zh: 休息过后我们可以回来，我们将解开王子与高塔之谜。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: We are poised to solve the mystery of the princes and their tower.
sentences.zh: 我们正准备解开王子与高塔之谜。

sentences.en: So Richard III has been crowned on the 6th of July.
sentences.zh: 所以理查三世已经在7月6日加冕了。

sentences.en: His two nephews did not turn up at the coronation.
sentences.zh: 他的两个侄子没有出席加冕典礼。

sentences.en: We know that that summer, they are seen playing in the gardens at the Tower of London complex.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那个夏天，有人看到他们在伦敦塔建筑群的花园里玩耍。

sentences.en: A prison is part of it, but it's not just a prison.
sentences.zh: 监狱是其中一部分，但它不仅仅是一座监狱。

sentences.en: It's a kind of royal complex.
sentences.zh: 它是一个某种皇家建筑群。

sentences.en: They are seen practising archery.
sentences.zh: 有人看到他们在练习射箭。

sentences.en: There is talk of faces at windows.
sentences.zh: 有人谈论窗户里有人脸。

sentences.en: But at some point that summer, their household servants are dismissed.
sentences.zh: 但在那个夏天的某个时候，他们的家仆被解雇了。

sentences.en: And then they are never seen again.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就再也没有出现过。

sentences.en: So, Tom, I mean, this is the key question.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我的意思是，这是核心问题。

sentences.en: What happens to them?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么了？

sentences.en: So we've got the question from Megan Young.
sentences.zh: 所以我们收到了梅根·杨的问题。

sentences.en: Do you think the princes were murdered?
sentences.zh: 你认为王子们被谋杀了吗？

sentences.en: And if so, when and by whom?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，是什么时候，又是谁干的？

sentences.en: I would have thought the overwhelming probability is that they were murdered and that it was done on Richard's orders.
sentences.zh: 我本以为极大的可能是他们被谋杀了，而且是奉理查之命干的。

sentences.en: And absolute certainty on this obviously is impossible because otherwise people wouldn't be debating it to this day.
sentences.zh: 对此绝对确定显然是不可能的，否则人们今天就不会还在争论了。

sentences.en: So we're not going to solve it because no definitive solution is ultimately possible.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会解开这个谜团，因为最终不可能有明确的答案。

sentences.en: But I think the overwhelming probability is that they were murdered and Richard did it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为极大的可能是他们被谋杀了，而且是理查干的。

sentences.en: So let's look at the other candidate.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们看看另一个候选人。

sentences.en: Go on then.
sentences.zh: 说下去吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The other major candidate.
sentences.zh: 另一个主要候选人。

sentences.en: He was the only one candidate, I would say, other than Richard, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 我想除了理查，他就是唯一的候选人了，对吧？

sentences.en: Wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Which would be Buckingham.
sentences.zh: 那就是白金汉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 同上。

sentences.en: So Buckingham is constable of England.
sentences.zh: 所以白金汉是英格兰的治安官。

sentences.en: He has been rewarded.
sentences.zh: 他得到了奖赏。

sentences.en: So he might conceivably have access to the tower.
sentences.zh: 因此他完全有可能接近高塔。

sentences.en: Yeah, because that's the key, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，因为这才是关键，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's the key.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键。

sentences.en: It's very hard to see how he has access without Richard's knowledge because Richard is the king.
sentences.zh: 很难想象他在理查不知情的情况下如何接近，因为理查是国王。

sentences.en: He, his men control everything.
sentences.zh: 他的人控制着一切。

sentences.en: So to me, it's hard to see how Buckingham and also the, so Buckingham is the, we open this episode with the quotation from The Daughter of Time by Josephine Tay.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，很难看出白金汉怎么能——而且，所以白金汉是——我们在本集开头引用了约瑟芬·铁伊的《时间的女儿》中的名言。

sentences.en: In Josephine Tay's book, her detective, Alan Grant, is laid up in hospital with a broken leg and he falls to solving the mystery of the princes in their town.
sentences.zh: 在约瑟芬·铁伊的书里，她的侦探艾伦·格兰特因断腿躺在医院里，开始着手解决王子与高塔之谜。

sentences.en: And he reads all the evidence and he decides that Buckingham did it.
sentences.zh: 他阅读了所有的证据，并断定是白金汉干的。

sentences.en: And Richard's enthusiasts have often thought that Buckingham did it.
sentences.zh: 理查的狂热崇拜者们经常认为是白金汉干的。

sentences.en: So there's a, there's a really brilliant book, which I loved when I was about 12, a great biography of Richard III, the,
sentences.zh: 所以有一本非常棒的书，我大约12岁时特别喜欢，是一本关于理查三世的伟大传记，由——

sentences.en: probably the definitive one for a lot of Ricardians by American academic called Paul Murray Kendall.
sentences.zh: 对许多理查三世拥护者来说，这可能是美国学者保罗·默里·肯德尔写的决定性传记。

sentences.en: And he has this big appendix in which he also thinks that Buckingham did it.
sentences.zh: 他有一个长长的附录，其中他也认为白金汉是凶手。

sentences.en: And he sort of says Buckingham had his, was playing a long game.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上说白金汉在下一盘大棋。

sentences.en: He had his eye on the throne.
sentences.zh: 他一直盯着王位。

sentences.en: He probably acted without Richard knowing.
sentences.zh: 他可能在理查不知情的情况下擅自行动。

sentences.en: He had access to the tower.
sentences.zh: 他能够进入塔楼。

sentences.en: I ultimately find that a bit implausible.
sentences.zh: 我最终觉得这有点难以置信。

sentences.en: I think Richard is so clearly the man in charge.
sentences.zh: 我认为理查显然才是当权者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he's the obvious person with most gain.
sentences.zh: 而且他是显而易见获益最多的人。

sentences.en: And again, I mean, it would be like if, if Buckingham were responsible, it would be in the way that Richard would have been responsible for the murder of Henry VI,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我的意思是，如果白金汉是幕后黑手，这就好比理查原本要为亨利六世的谋杀负责一样，

sentences.en: i.e. not ultimately because it was Edward IV.
sentences.zh: 也就是说最终不用负责，因为那是爱德华四世干的。

sentences.en: The buck stops with the king.
sentences.zh: 最终责任在国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the sort of counter argument, we should, we should, the counter argument is Tom,
sentences.zh: 反面论点是，我们应该——我们应该讲讲反面论点，汤姆，

sentences.en: that Richard is weakened by the deaths of the two boys because people hold it against him and he doesn't immediately gain anything by it.
sentences.zh: 那就是理查因两个男孩的死而势力减弱，因为人们将此归咎于他，而且他并没有从中直接获得任何好处。

sentences.en: But I would say in answer to that, there is the first revolt, isn't there, in late July.
sentences.zh: 但作为回应，我要说的是，七月下旬不是爆发了第一次叛乱吗？

sentences.en: So within a month of his coronation, there is an attempt by some conspirators to rescue the two boys and to stage a sort of pro-Woodville counter coup.
sentences.zh: 因此在他的加冕礼不到一个月内，一些阴谋家试图营救这两个男孩，并策划了一场亲伍德ville的反政变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I mean, all, everything you know about thousands of years of history is that when that kind of thing happens, the person in charge decides usually will get rid of the focus of,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于几千年历史你所知道的一切都表明，当那种事情发生时，当权者通常会决定除掉阻碍的焦点——

sentences.en: of, of resistance.
sentences.zh: 也就是反抗的焦点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, get rid of the alternative candidates.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，除掉替代人选。

sentences.en: That's what dictators, kings, emperors have done throughout all history.
sentences.zh: 这就是独裁者、国王、皇帝在整个历史上一直都在做的事。

sentences.en: So it would make complete sense for Richard at that point to say, oh my God, they've got to go.
sentences.zh: 所以对理查来说，当时说“天哪，他们必须得走”是完全合乎逻辑的。

sentences.en: I can't keep having these revolts.
sentences.zh: 我不能总是应付这些叛乱。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's because he's evil and malignant.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是因为他邪恶阴险。

sentences.en: I just think that's because he thinks-
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得是因为他认为——

sentences.en: He's hard-headed.
sentences.zh: 他很务实。

sentences.en: It's realpolitik.
sentences.zh: 这就是现实政治。

sentences.en: It's a calculus of power.
sentences.zh: 这是一场权力的算计。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think the other, the other thing that militates against the idea that Buckingham did it is that Richard actually had the perfect, I mean,
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个——另一个反驳白金汉是凶手的论点是，理查实际上拥有完美的——我的意思是，

sentences.en: the problem for Richard is that people are starting to say they've been murdered.
sentences.zh: 理查面临的问题是人们开始说他们被谋杀了。

sentences.en: So the obvious way to counter that is to produce them.
sentences.zh: 所以反驳这一说法的显而易见的方法就是把他们带出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So if you can't produce them, that is very, very suspicious, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你无法让他们露面，我认为这非常非常可疑。

sentences.en: Um, if they're dead, you can't produce them, then obviously the idea would be to try and blame someone for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他们死了，你无法让他们露面，那么显而易见的主意就是试图把罪名嫁祸给某人。

sentences.en: And the ideal opportunity takes place when Buckingham, who has not been rewarded as he feels fit, joins in a rebellion that aims to bring Henry Tudor,
sentences.zh: 而绝佳的机会发生在白金汉身上，他觉得自己没有得到应得的奖赏，于是加入了一场旨在将亨利·都铎——

sentences.en: the only conceivable Lancastrian claimant, to the throne.
sentences.zh: 唯一的兰开斯特家族合法王位继承人——推上王位的叛乱。

sentences.en: Um, and, and this revolt is defeated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且这场叛乱被镇压了。

sentences.en: Um, Buckingham is captured.
sentences.zh: 嗯，白金汉被捕了。

sentences.en: He is taken to Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 他被带到索尔兹伯里。

sentences.en: He is taken to a courtyard between the Blue Boar Inn and the Saracens' head inn.
sentences.zh: 他被带到蓝野猪客栈和萨拉森之头客栈之间的一个庭院。

sentences.en: Uh, off with his head, so much for Buckingham in the famous cry of, of Richard III in Shakespeare's play.
sentences.zh: 呃，“砍下他的头，白金汉到此为止”，这是莎士比亚戏剧中理查三世著名的呐喊。

sentences.en: Um, and Buckingham's head is severed in, I think I've already mentioned this, what becomes the laundry department of Debenhams in Salisbury, which has sadly since closed.
sentences.zh: 呃，白金汉的头被砍了下来，我想我已经提过了，那地方后来成了索尔兹伯里德本汉姆百货公司的洗衣部，可惜现在已经关门了。

sentences.en: A lovely detail.
sentences.zh: 一个可爱的细节。

sentences.en: But for a long time, um, you know, you go in to buy a bra and, whoa, Dick Buckingham would pop up carrying his head.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，你知道，你去买胸罩，哇，迪克·白金汉会提着他的头突然冒出来。

sentences.en: Well, you know what Richard said about Buckingham's Rebels?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道理查是怎么评价白金汉的叛军的吗？

sentences.en: He said they were horrible adulterers and boards.
sentences.zh: 他说他们是可怕的通奸犯和伪君子。

sentences.en: So in a way, they're kind of ladies' underwear department of a, of a mid-market department store.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，他们有点像中端百货公司里的女装内衣部。

sentences.en: Very fitting.
sentences.zh: 非常贴切。

sentences.en: Makes complete, yeah.
sentences.zh: 完全说得通，是的。

sentences.en: So, so Buckingham's, Buckingham's died a traitor.
sentences.zh: 所以，白金汉，白金汉作为叛徒死了。

sentences.en: So it's the perfect opportunity for Richard to say, oh, well, Buckingham did it.
sentences.zh: 所以对理查德来说，这是一个绝佳的机会，可以顺水推舟地说，哦，好吧，是白金汉干的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但他没有这么做。

sentences.en: No, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: I mean, the other candidate that sometimes people, so I've been to the Richard III experience, or whatever it's called, in Leicester.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们有时会提到的另一个嫌疑人——我也去过莱斯特的理查德三世体验馆，或者不管它叫什么。

sentences.en: And you can vote.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以投票。

sentences.en: There's a sort of interactive element where you can vote about who you think did it.
sentences.zh: 那里有一种互动环节，你可以投票选出你认为是谁干的。

sentences.en: Um, Richard Buckingham or Henry Tudor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，理查德、白金汉还是亨利·都铎。

sentences.en: And some people say Henry Tudor killed them.
sentences.zh: 有些人说亨利·都铎杀了他们。

sentences.en: Uh, very, very ardent Ricardians sometimes say this.
sentences.zh: 呃，非常非常狂热的理查德三世拥护者有时会这么说。

sentences.en: But again, I think that's very, very implausible.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我认为这非常非常不可信。

sentences.en: Because I think...
sentences.zh: 因为我认为……

sentences.en: Well, Margaret Beaufort, his mother, is another candidate, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，玛格丽特·博福特，他的母亲，是另一个嫌疑人，对吧？

sentences.en: What have they been doing in the, you know, what have the kids been doing in the interim?
sentences.zh: 他们在……你知道的，这段时间孩子们都在干什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you the other thing about Margaret Beaufort, uh, who, who's Henry Tudor's mother, um, is that she reached, she reaches an accommodation with Elizabeth Woodville,
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于玛格丽特·博福特——亨利·都铎的母亲，呃——我还要告诉你一件事，那就是她与伊丽莎白·伍德维尔达成了一项妥协，

sentences.en: who's still in, in Sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 后者当时仍然在避难所里。

sentences.en: And the only conceivable reason for that is that they would both, you know, that they would have for that, is that Elizabeth Woodville assumes that her children are dead.
