sentences.zh: 但这个位于偏僻之地的教堂内部的发现，就在达特穆尔中心，

sentences.en: end of a lane, are extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 一条小路的尽头，是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: The evidence suggests that Edward was, so that's Edward V, so the elder of the princes.
sentences.zh: 证据表明爱德华——也就是爱德华五世，也就是年长的那个王子。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, I think, Dominic, that all the pretenders, none of them are Edward V.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我觉得很有趣的是，所有的伪王，没有一个是爱德华五世。

sentences.en: They're all kind of Richard.
sentences.zh: 他们全都是理查之类的人。

sentences.en: Well, probably because he was too well-known at the age of 12.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可能是因为他在12岁时就太知名了。

sentences.en: So you can't impersonate him.
sentences.zh: 所以你无法冒充他。

sentences.en: So the evidence suggests that Edward was actually sent to live out his days on his half-brother's land as long as he kept quiet,
sentences.zh: 因此，证据表明爱德华实际上被送往他异母兄弟的土地上度过余生，只要他保持沉默，

sentences.en: as part of a deal reached between his mother and Richard III and later with Henry Tudor.
sentences.zh: 作为他母亲与理查三世以及后来与亨利·都铎达成协议的一部分。

sentences.en: Once you take all the clues together, it does appear that the story of the princes in the tower may need to be rewritten.
sentences.zh: 一旦把所有的线索联系在一起，塔中王子们的历史确实似乎需要被重写。

sentences.en: Well, you know what he would call himself, according to this?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道根据这个，他会怎么称呼自己吗？

sentences.en: John Evans.
sentences.zh: 约翰·埃文斯。

sentences.en: And there's...
sentences.zh: 而且有……

sentences.en: He built his own chantry, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他给自己建了一座小教堂，不是吗？

sentences.en: At the age of 41.
sentences.zh: 在41岁的时候。

sentences.en: And he put lots of clues to himself.
sentences.zh: 他留下了很多关于他自己的线索。

sentences.en: Well, among which, on his tomb, of course, if you look at Evans, what were the first two letters of Evans?
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中之一，在墓碑上，当然，如果你看埃文斯（Evans），埃文斯的前两个字母是什么？

sentences.en: E.V.
sentences.zh: E.V.

sentences.en: E.V.
sentences.zh: E.V.

sentences.en: Oh, extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 哦，太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: Well, well.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: Do you believe this, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你相信这个吗？

sentences.en: I'm not entirely convinced.
sentences.zh: 我并不完全信服。

sentences.en: I'm not convinced at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不信服。

sentences.en: When John Dyke says that it sounds somewhat like the Da Vinci Code, I think that's...
sentences.zh: 当约翰·戴克说这听起来有点像《达·芬奇密码》时，我认为这……

sentences.en: I think that's not inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这并没说错。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, let me just address the central implausibility.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，让我来谈谈核心的不可信之处。

sentences.en: Is it plausible that Richard, who we know is so hard-nosed...
sentences.zh: 理查是我们所知道的那种如此精明强干的人……这合理吗？

sentences.en: And Henry VII is equally a bastard.
sentences.zh: 亨利七世同样是个混蛋。

sentences.en: And so two incredibly ruthless men who have a track record of executing their enemies, which is why they're able to become king in the first place, that they would agree a deal
sentences.zh: 所以两个极其冷酷无情、有着处决政敌记录的人——这也是他们当初能够当上国王的原因——他们会达成一项协议，

sentences.en: to allow their biggest rival to go and live under an assumed name on Dartmoor.
sentences.zh: 允许他们最大的竞争对手去达特穆尔化名生活。

sentences.en: And that he then, in his turn...
sentences.zh: 然后他反过来……

sentences.en: Which would leave lots of clues.
sentences.zh: 这会留下许多线索。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Would never surface and try and recapture the crown, but would build a load of clues into the church.
sentences.zh: 绝不会露面并试图夺回王位，而是在教堂里埋下一堆线索。

sentences.en: Which, I think that's just, you know...
sentences.zh: 我觉得这简直就是，你知道……

sentences.en: I mean, stranger things have happened, but not many.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，更奇怪的事也发生过，但不多。

sentences.en: That's all I'll say.
sentences.zh: 我就说这么多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I mean, Philippa Langley, you know, she was right with the car park, so...
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我的意思是，菲莉帕·兰利，你知道，她在停车场这件事上猜对了，所以……

sentences.en: She was.
sentences.zh: 她确实猜对了。

sentences.en: She wasn't it.
sentences.zh: 不是吗。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: She'll be laughing at us one day, Tom.
sentences.zh: 总有一天她会在嘲笑我们，汤姆。

sentences.en: In that Channel 4 documentary, proving that Edward V...
sentences.zh: 在第四频道的那部纪录片里，证明了爱德华五世……

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: They'll play bits of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们会播放这段播客的片段。

sentences.en: They're a kind of montage of our shamed countenances.
sentences.zh: 播放我们那些羞愧面孔的剪辑。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Anyway, Ping Pong on the Discord asked, why are we still interested in this mystery murder over so many others?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，Discord上的“乒乓”问道，为什么我们对这起谋杀之谜的兴趣超过了其他那么多谜团？

sentences.en: Well, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And I think, actually, it is because there are juSt...
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，实际上，正是因为有……

sentences.en: A final solution, I think, isn't...
sentences.zh: 一个最终的解决方案，我认为，不是……

sentences.en: I shouldn't use the word final solution, should I actually...
sentences.zh: 我不该用“最终解决方案”这个词，对吧……

sentences.en: The kind of conclusive solution is not possible because...
sentences.zh: 那种确凿的解决方案是不可能的，因为……

sentences.en: Yeah, agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，同意。

sentences.en: There's not enough evidence.
sentences.zh: 证据不足。

sentences.en: We can't be...
sentences.zh: 我们不能……

sentences.en: I mean, even though we both think that Richard did it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尽管我们俩都认为理查是凶手。

sentences.en: But there's enough evidence to construct all kinds of various possibilities.
sentences.zh: 但有足够的证据来构建各种各样的可能性。

sentences.en: Plus, of course, it involves King.
sentences.zh: 另外，当然，这还涉及国王。

sentences.en: But also, clearly, there's a romantic element, isn't there, to the last Plantagenet, to Richard III, which encourages Ricardians to find him innocent.
sentences.zh: 但显然，对于最后一个金雀花王朝，对于理查三世，有一种浪漫主义色彩，不是吗？这鼓励了理查三世的拥护者们去认定他是无辜的。

sentences.en: So there's this sort of notion, isn't there, that the medieval period comes to a kind of crashing end of the Battle of Bosworth.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一种观念，不是吗：中世纪在博斯沃思战役中迎来了一个轰然破碎的结局。

sentences.en: Plus, Henry's kind of accountant, a grim accountant.
sentences.zh: 再加上，亨利有点像个会计师，一个冷酷的会计师。

sentences.en: The age of knights and stuff is gone, and it's replaced by, exactly, this sort of miserable penny pincher and then his wail of a son.
sentences.zh: 骑士的时代等等已经一去不复返了，取而代之的是，没错，这种讨价还价的吝啬鬼，然后是他那个像哭丧鬼一样的儿子。

sentences.en: And that people romanticise the age that went before the Plantagenets.
sentences.zh: 人们将金雀花王朝之前的时代浪漫化了。

sentences.en: They romanticise Richard, of course, because he's the guy from the north.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们将理查浪漫化，因为他是来自北方的人。

sentences.en: He's very religious.
sentences.zh: 他非常虔诚。

sentences.en: All of this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And I think then there becomes this urge to find him innocent and also to think, I would say,
sentences.zh: 我想随后就会产生一种冲动，想要证明他是无辜的，并且还认为，我想说，

sentences.en: to think that you have discovered the key to history and something that the academics haven't spotted and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 认为自己发现了历史的关键，发现了学者们没有注意到的东西，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I think, just wondering about this, just thinking aloud here, I wonder also if a part of it isn't sublimated hostility to Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 我想，仅仅是琢磨这个，在这里自言自语，我也在想，其中一部分会不会是对莎士比亚潜意识里的敌意？

sentences.en: I didn't see that coming.
sentences.zh: 我没想到会这样。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Well, there is actually kind of rather similar stuff around the identity of Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上围绕莎士比亚的身份也有类似的情况。

sentences.en: You know, was he the Earl of Oxford or whatever?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是牛津伯爵还是别的什么人？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So there's a question here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有个问题。

sentences.en: Olly Oco, again, on the Discord.
sentences.zh: 奥利·奥科（Olly Oco），同样是在Discord上。

sentences.en: Was Shakespeare's reputation slipping circa 1593 and he needed a sycophantic pro-tudor play to keep the Queen happy and boost his standard in court?
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚在大约1593年的声誉是不是在下滑，他需要一部谄媚的亲都铎戏剧来让女王高兴并提升他在宫廷中的地位？

sentences.en: Oh, there's somebody who doesn't like Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 哦，这里有人不喜欢莎士比亚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think that this idea that Shakespeare is a kind of, he's either, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种想法认为莎士比亚是一种，他要么，你知道，

sentences.en: he's a fraud who is taking the credit that she properly belongs to an aristocrat or that he's a kind of sinister, conniving sycophant.
sentences.zh: 他是一个骗子，窃取了本该属于贵族的荣誉，或者他是一个阴险、圆滑的马屁精。

sentences.en: It kind of, maybe if you had a bad time studying him at school or something, it's a way to kind of elbow him aside.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，也许如果你在学校里学他时有一段糟糕的经历什么的，这是一种把他挤开的方式。

sentences.en: Is it not just a hostility to the received wisdom in general and just sort of the idea of authority?
sentences.zh: 这难道不只是对普遍共识的敌意以及对权威的想法吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I think it's a part of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think Shakespeare is kind of, you know, as the greatest writer.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为莎士比亚某种程度上，你知道，作为最伟大的作家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a kind of pleasure in kicking him.
sentences.zh: 踢他一脚有一种快感。

sentences.en: I think there's definitely a lot of people who get a lot of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我觉得绝对有很多人能从中获得很多乐趣。

sentences.en: So in The Daughter of Time, Thomas More is absolutely the villain.
sentences.zh: 所以在《时间的女儿》中，托马斯·莫尔绝对是个反派。

sentences.en: You know, you get that in, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在书中也能看到这一点，你知道的。

sentences.en: Hilary Mantel.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·曼特尔。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: She thinks Thomas More is the villain.
sentences.zh: 她认为托马斯·莫尔是反派。

sentences.en: So Thomas More and Shakespeare are both, you know, people who've been so eulogised that there's a kind of seditious pleasure in giving them a kicking.
sentences.zh: 所以托马斯·莫尔和莎士比亚都是，你知道的，被赞誉备至的人，以至于狠狠抨击他们有一种煽动性的快乐。

sentences.en: But I think, I do also think that Richard's obviously been unlucky in Shakespeare because it's a brilliant play.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我也确实认为理查在莎士比亚笔下显然很不走运，因为这是一部精彩的戏剧。

sentences.en: The Ian McKellen play, have you seen the?
sentences.zh: 伊恩·麦克莱恩的那部剧，你看过吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, fantastic.
sentences.zh: 看过了，太棒了。

sentences.en: Set in sort of World War II type.
sentences.zh: 背景设定在二战类型的时代。

sentences.en: Yes, it's kind of 1930s.
sentences.zh: 是的，有点像20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: A bit like the production of Beckett that I did at the Edinburgh Festival, Tom.
sentences.zh: 有点像我在爱丁堡艺术节上制作的贝克特戏剧，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes, it all becomes fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，这一切都变成了法西斯式的。

sentences.en: I think there's a kind of way in which you could cast Richard as a kind of Raul Castro or, you know, the brother of, you know, an autocrat or, you know, one of those,
sentences.zh: 我想你可以把理查塑造成劳尔·卡斯特罗那样的人，或者你知道的，某个独裁者的兄弟，或者你知道的，那种人，

sentences.en: one of the Al-Assads or something.
sentences.zh: 阿萨德家族的人或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: You know, someone who, after the charismatic founder of the regime has gone, has to be ruthless to keep his regime in power.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种在政权的富有魅力的创立者离去后，必须心狠手辣才能维持政权的人。

sentences.en: To keep Jim Callaghan to Edward IV's Harold Wilson.
sentences.zh: 就像把吉姆·卡拉汉比作爱德华四世的哈罗德·威尔逊。

sentences.en: That's the other way.
sentences.zh: 那是另一种方式。

sentences.en: Is that the comparison you were looking for?
sentences.zh: 这就是你在寻找的比较吗？

sentences.en: That's the comparison that I was griping for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直想找的比较。

sentences.en: I'm glad that you've provided it.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你给出了这个对比。

sentences.en: Well, he's Robert Kennedy to JFK, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他是肯尼迪（JFK）的罗伯特·肯尼迪。

sentences.en: I think he's more serious.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他更严肃。

sentences.en: He's the dutiful younger brother who finds himself pushed suddenly into the limelight.
sentences.zh: 他是那个听话的弟弟，发现自己突然被推到了聚光灯下。

sentences.en: But Robert Kennedy didn't.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯特·肯尼迪可没有。

sentences.en: Didn't murder any children.
sentences.zh: 没有谋杀任何儿童。

sentences.en: No, I mean, that's true.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，这倒没错。

sentences.en: We can't conclusively say that Richard did.
sentences.zh: 我们不能斩钉截铁地说理查干过。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: You see, I think, Tom, I'm very sympathetic to Richard.
sentences.zh: 你看，汤姆，我对理查很同情。

sentences.en: But even though I think he probably did kill the princess in the tower.
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为他可能确实杀害了塔中的王子。

sentences.en: I think he's in a really, really difficult position and he's trying to make the best of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他处在一个非常非常困难的境地，他正在努力做到最好。

sentences.en: And of course, killing your nephews is not normally the most admirable way out.
sentences.zh: 当然，杀死你的侄子通常不是最令人钦佩的出路。

sentences.en: But I think to be brutal about it, in that world.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得说得残酷一点，在那个世界里。

sentences.en: He had no choice.
sentences.zh: 他别无选择。

sentences.en: His choice is probably keep taking these bloodstained acts or basically to lose the game.
sentences.zh: 他的选择可能是继续采取这些血腥的行径，或者基本上就是输掉这场博弈。

sentences.en: But he did lose the game.
sentences.zh: 但他确实输掉了博弈。

sentences.en: And he lost the game, not just for himself, but for his entire family.
sentences.zh: 他不仅为自己输掉了博弈，也为他的整个家族输掉了。

sentences.en: The Yorkists should have, you know, there was a plenitude of sons and daughters.
sentences.zh: 约克家族本应该，你知道的，有大量的儿子和女儿。

sentences.en: Because they should have, you know, the 16th century should have been the Yorkist age.
sentences.zh: 因为他们本该，你知道的，16世纪本该是约克家族的时代。

sentences.en: And the fact that it wasn't, Richard could have taken very, very different decisions.
sentences.zh: 然而事实并非如此，理查本可以做出非常、非常不同的决定。

sentences.en: The interesting thing is that had there been the Yorkist age, I mean, this is indulging in a colossal counterfactual,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，如果曾经有过约克王朝时期，我的意思是，这是一种巨大的历史反事实假设，

sentences.en: which I know we've poured scorn on in earlier podcasts, the idea of counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们在之前的播客中对反事实假设这种想法嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: But a secure Yorkist regime, a Plantagenet regime in the mid-16th century, I would say, is much less likely to break with Rome and to encourage the growth of Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，一个稳固的约克王朝政权，一个在16世纪中叶的金雀花政权，断绝与罗马教廷关系的并发起新教发展的可能性要小得多。

sentences.en: And it's partly Henry VIII's insecurity, famously.
sentences.zh: 部分原因正如众人所知，是亨利八世的不安全感。

sentences.en: Although it's obvious that, you know, having unsuitable marriages is something that Henry VIII is capable of passing on to his descendants.
sentences.zh: 尽管很明显，你知道，拥有不合适的婚姻是亨利八世能够传递给他的后代的一大特点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以谁知道呢？

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: So maybe his grandson or some successor would have been Henry VIII and the different guys.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他的孙子或其他继任者也会像亨利八世和那些不同的人一样。

sentences.en: So I do think Richard is a tragic figure and not for the reasons that Shakespeare makes him a tragic figure.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为理查德是一个悲剧人物，但原因并非莎士比亚将他塑造成悲剧人物的那样。

sentences.en: He's not a kind of out-and-out villain.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种彻头彻尾的恶棍。

sentences.en: I think he, perhaps for reasons that ultimately he's unable to control, he destroys himself and his family and his regime.
sentences.zh: 我认为，也许由于最终无法控制的原因，他毁灭了自己、他的家族和他的政权。

sentences.en: And he's a massive loser.
sentences.zh: 而且他是个彻头彻尾的失败者。

sentences.en: Harsh.
sentences.zh: 真严厉。

sentences.en: Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: He's a murderer and a loser.
sentences.zh: 他是个杀人犯和失败者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Very harsh.
sentences.zh: 太严厉了。

sentences.en: I shall leave you to field the correspondence with the Ricardians when the podcast is over.
sentences.zh: 播客结束后，理查德三世拥护者的来信就交给你来应付了。

sentences.en: Please address your complaints to Tom and not to me.
sentences.zh: 请将您的投诉发给汤姆，而不是我。

sentences.en: So who do you think murdered the Prince of the Town before we go?
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，你认为是谁谋杀了城里的王子？

sentences.en: Well, I think Richard did it, but I think he was right to do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为是理查德干的，但我认为他这么做是对的。

sentences.en: That's the difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是区别所在。

sentences.en: But he wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 但他做的不对。

sentences.en: He immolated his regime.
sentences.zh: 他断送了自己的政权。

sentences.en: Well, if he'd won at Bosworth, though, Tom, if he'd won at Bosworth, it would have been right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他在博斯沃思赢了的话，汤姆，如果他在博斯沃思赢了，那就是对的。

sentences.en: He didn't, did he?
sentences.zh: 但他没赢，不是吗？

sentences.en: He didn't because nobody backed him.
sentences.zh: 他没赢是因为没有人支持他。

sentences.en: Well, he was pretty close at Bosworth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在博斯沃思离胜利很近。

sentences.en: I mean, it was very much a, you know, it was a bit like Aston Villa's exit from the FA Cup last night, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很像，你知道的，这有点像阿斯顿维拉昨晚足总杯出局，汤姆。

sentences.en: It could have gone either way.
sentences.zh: 胜负本来很难说。

sentences.en: Sorry, I know that's a sore point.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我知道这是一个痛处。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Which we will see, what will we see them for next?
sentences.zh: 接下来我们会看到什么，我们将为了什么再次见面？

sentences.en: Railways.
sentences.zh: 铁路。

sentences.en: History of the Railways.
sentences.zh: 铁路史。

sentences.en: Beginnings of the Railways.
sentences.zh: 铁路的起源。

sentences.en: History of the Railways.
sentences.zh: 铁路史。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 令人兴奋。

sentences.en: In which Dan Jackson, I believe, may be wearing a hat.
sentences.zh: 届时丹·杰克逊，我相信，可能会戴着一顶帽子。

sentences.en: He does, but of course you won't be able to see that.
sentences.zh: 他戴了，但你当然看不见。

sentences.en: No, but you'll know that it was there.
sentences.zh: 不，但你会知道它在那儿。

sentences.en: All right, so we'll see you then.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们到时候见。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢收听。

sentences.en: And don't forget that Dominic also thinks that Richard murdered the Princess of the Tower.
sentences.zh: 别忘了多米尼克也认为理查德谋杀了塔中的王子。

sentences.en: So address all correspondence to both of us.
sentences.zh: 所以请把所有的信件发给我们俩。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。
